crossRefs.note: A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to sleep:
so your poverty will come as a robber, and your scarcity as an armed man.
The slothful man doesn’t roast his game, but the possessions of diligent men are prized.
The soul of the sluggard desires, and has nothing, but the desire of the diligent shall be fully satisfied.
The sluggard will not plow by reason of the winter; therefore he shall beg in harvest, and have nothing.
a little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to sleep,
so your poverty will come as a robber and your want as an armed man.
Why should I take my flesh in my teeth, and put my life in my hand?
The merciful man does good to his own soul, but he who is cruel troubles his own flesh.
One will devour on the right hand, and be hungry; and he will eat on the left hand, and they will not be satisfied.…

translations.web: The fool folds his hands together and ruins himself.
translations.bsb: The fool folds his hands and consumes his own flesh.
translations.kjv: The fool foldeth his hands together, and eateth his own flesh.
translations.asv: The fool foldeth his hands together, and eateth his own flesh.
